brief: A tool caddy with a carry handle and divided bins for screws and bits.

requirements.evidence: Three hex base cells in a row: piece:-1,0,0 (full), piece:0,0,0 (full), piece:1,0,0 (full), with closed faces and joints locked (capOpenFaces, lockJoints). check_build is clean, meshClash clear.
Handle on a top cover of the west cell (cover:-1,0,0;full;top, handle:-1,0,0;top) with inserts; it sits over an empty cell so it does not block the bins.

requirements.requirement: Divided bins for screws and bits
requirements.evidence: bin:0,0,0 is hex-bin-full-div3 (3 compartments) for screws, with M3 screw props in its compartments; bin:1,0,0 is hex-bin-full-div2 (2 compartments) for bits.
The 2-compartment bit bin is empty: a hex key prop would not rest in it (cell wall overlap), so no bits are shown in it.
The configurator checks fit and collisions only; it cannot verify strength, load rating or material for carrying tools.

finish.summary: Built a three-cell tool caddy: two divided bins (3-compartment for screws, 2-compartment for bits) side by side, a carry handle on a top cover of the third cell, and all open faces capped with joints locked. check_build is clean with meshClash clear. Three screw props sit in the screw bin, though the compartment props are flagged PROP_BELOW_RIM (they sit under the rim, so they are hard to see). The bit bin is empty. Material strength for carrying weight is not verified by the configurator.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
